Ilow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Iłów, Poland

Not demolished. Iłów, first mentioned in 1224 as a land grant to Cistercian monks and formally chartered as a noble town in 1506, saw Jewish settlement from 1680, with synagogue-building rights granted in 1750. The community grew from 106 in 1764 to 70% of the population (258 people) by 1857, still 48% (374 people) in 1921. Notable native son Lejb Sonder (Aleksander Sochaczewski), a painter sentenced to 20 years in Siberian exile for participating in the January Uprising, was born here in 1843. This cemetery, likely established in the late 18th century northeast of the market square, was destroyed during WWII when Germans used its tombstones to pave sidewalks; the site remains unmarked today.
